title: Underived closed-support Hom sequence on injective sheaves
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, i:D -> T a closed immersion and v:V -> T its complementary open immersion. For the natural restriction map tau:Gamma(T,-) -> Gamma(V,v^*(-)), there is a natural A-linear alpha:Hom_T(i_* A_D,-) -> Gamma(T,-), with alpha followed by tau zero, such that 0 -> Hom_T(i_* A_D,J) -> Gamma(T,J) -> Gamma(V,v^*J) -> 0 is short exact whenever J is injective. The functors use [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]; injectivity is [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Proof steps 1 and 3; Stacks Etale Cohomology Tag 095L and Modules on Sites Tag 03DI

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to the constant rank-one A-module sheaf. The canonical pullback isomorphisms of constant sheaves identify its quotient with i_* A_D and its first term with v_! A_V. These are isomorphisms of the fixed-coefficient ModuleCat-valued sheaf category; no ringed sheaf comparison is needed.

The constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction and evaluation at 1 give an A-linear isomorphism Hom(A_T,J) = Gamma(T,J), natural in J. Precomposition with A_T -> i_* A_D gives alpha. The extension-by-zero adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] similarly identifies Hom(v_! A_V,J) with Gamma(V,v^*J). Compatibility of the units under uniqueness of adjoints identifies the second map with the prescribed globalSectionsUpperStarMap, so its composition with alpha is zero. The transported adjunction unit is computed using Mathlib's public Adjunction.ofNatIsoRight_unit and component/whiskering formulas; no duplicate unit lemma is introduced.

For an injective target J, Hom(-,J) takes the coefficient short exact sequence to a short exact sequence of A-modules: precomposition with its epimorphism is injective; maps annihilating its first arrow descend uniquely through the cokernel; injectivity of J extends every morphism along its first monomorphism. Transport this sequence across the three linear identifications. Empty open or closed schemes and the zero ring give the same argument.

proof_origin.place: Proof steps 1 and 3, expanded into linear adjunctions and the injective extension property
